queries.query: large language model OR LLM "network configuration" OR "network config" "natural language" "intent to configuration"
queries.rationale: Locate work where LLMs or generative models translate operator intent / NL into router/switch configurations or CLI sequences (direct relevance to NetOps automation and intent-driven networking).

queries.query: LLM hallucination misconfiguration "network" OR "NetOps" "hallucination" OR "fabrication" OR "incorrect"
queries.rationale: Identify documented failure modes where generative models produce incorrect or fabricated network artifacts (configs, commands, topology descriptions) and any analyses of causes.
source_preferences: operator blogs with reproducible examples (e.g., Cloud provider or large ISP engineering posts)

queries.rationale: Search for architectures combining generation + automated validation + repair loops applied to network configuration synthesis or remediation (architectural mitigations).

queries.query: network configuration verification formal tools "Batfish" "VeriFlow" "Anteater" "Header Space Analysis"
queries.rationale: Gather foundational and recent deterministic/network-verification tools and methods that can act as validators/verifiers for generated configs and provide operational correctness metrics.
source_preferences: project websites and code repos (Batfish, VeriFlow)

queries.rationale: Survey intent-based networking and policy-compilation work (mapping high-level intents to low-level configs) to position LLM-driven intent translation relative to established compilers.
source_preferences: industry whitepapers (Cisco, Juniper) with technical detail

queries.query: tool-assisted LLM self-correction "external verifier" "tool use" "LLM" network
queries.rationale: Find literature on LLMs using external tools/APIs/verifiers (tool use, ReAct, Toolformer) in the context of system operations and how that affects correctness and robustness.
source_preferences: systems conferences applying these methods to operations

queries.rationale: Locate approaches that bound the number/extent of self-corrections or enforce constraints during iterative repair—useful for safety in NetOps loops.

queries.query: AIOps "remediation" "automated repair" "fault localization" "root cause analysis" network
queries.rationale: Collect neighbouring AIOps literature on automated diagnosis and remediation (non-LLM and ML-based) to compare failure modes and evaluation practices.
source_preferences: industry symposia (CISCO Live, operator fora) with reproducible artifacts

queries.rationale: Survey existing benchmarks and suites used for evaluating models in networking/AIOps to assess task realism, metrics, and gaps in benchmark validity.
Find public datasets of network configurations, topologies, and change histories suitable for training/evaluating generative systems and verifiers.
Collect operationally meaningful correctness metrics used by verification tools and operators that can validate generated configs beyond syntactic correctness.

queries.query: emulation simulation platforms mininet ns-3 containerlab "network testbed" "batfish"
queries.rationale: Identify testbeds and emulation/simulation platforms for executing and validating configs and workflows in controlled environments.
source_preferences: software project sites (Mininet, ns-3, containerlab, VIRL)

queries.rationale: Broaden to agentic/operational-safety literature for autonomous agents executing critical infrastructure tasks, to import formal safety concepts and mitigations.
Find work on hybrid human–automation workflows, approval/rollback mechanisms, and guardrails for automated NetOps to evaluate practical mitigations.

queries.query: failure-mode analysis "misconfiguration" "outage" "LLM generated" network case study
queries.rationale: Search for empirical case studies and postmortems where automated or erroneous configurations caused outages, to ground threat modelling and realistic failure scenarios.

inclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed publications (conference, journal) and archival preprints (arXiv) with sufficient methodological detail.
Public datasets, benchmark repositories, and open-source implementations (GitHub, Zenodo) that enable reproduction or concrete evaluation.
Papers and tools explicitly applied to network configuration, verification, NetOps, AIOps, or operational agentic workflows.
Works proposing or evaluating mitigations, verifiers, or safety architectures for automated configuration or agentic actions.
Empirical case studies, postmortems, and reproducible incident analyses relevant to configuration-induced outages or operational failures.
Standards, IETF drafts, and industry technical whitepapers when they provide technical methods, APIs, or reproducible examples.
exclusion_criteria: Purely high-level marketing materials or vendor slides without technical details or reproducible artifacts.
Blog posts or news pieces that assert claims but lack reproducible methods or references (unless accompanied by code/datasets).
LLM/ML papers focused solely on linguistic benchmarks (GLUE, SQuAD) or unrelated NLP tasks with no operational NetOps mapping.
Proprietary datasets or closed-source tools that cannot be accessed or validated by reviewers (document their existence but exclude as primary evidence).
Works outside the network operations scope (e.g., unrelated cyber-security, hardware design) unless they present methods transferrable to NetOps verification.
date_rationale: Cover the formative literature for network verification and intent-based networking from roughly 2000–2018 (established formal tools and compilers) and comprehensively survey 2018–present (rise of large generative models, AIOps, and recent tool-assisted LLM methods). Searches should include the latest available work through the planned run date (covering up to the time of execution) to capture rapidly evolving LLM/agentic literature and the most recent benchmarks/datasets.
